items.name: Kitesurf intro lesson (Level 1 DISCOVER) at Ždrijac beach, Nin
items.driveFromVilla: 5.6 km, about 10 min (OSRM, to the Plaža Ždrijac polygon centre)
items.description: A 2-hour first lesson in the shallow Nin lagoon, about 10 minutes from the villa. It starts on land with kite control and moves into shallow water. It works well as a team afternoon because everyone starts at the same level, and the school is open every day from May to late October.

items.name: SUP Safari in the Nin lagoon
items.description: A guided 2-hour stand-up-paddle tour from the same beach as the kite school. It needs no wind and suits mixed-fitness teams, so it is the low-key option when the kite group is too large or the wind is wrong.

items.name: Nin Riviera 'Beach Olympics' plus BBQ evening

location.name: Nin Riviera sandy beaches (Ždrijac / Queen's Beach area)

items.driveFromVilla: 5.6 km, about 10 min to Ždrijac (OSRM); Queen's Beach is about 1.4 km, a 17-minute walk
items.description: The Zadar Region Tourist Board's own incentive format: beach volleyball, paddleboard races, kite-flying and sandcastle contests on Nin's sandy beaches with Velebit as the backdrop, followed by a BBQ. For a small team it can be self-run: games on the beach, then dinner at the villa's grill area.

items.name: Zrmanja river kayak tour (14 km, past the Veliki Buk waterfall)
items.driveFromVilla: 78.6 km, about 85 min (OSRM, to the Kaštel Žegarski village centroid)
items.description: The team paddles the official 14 km kayak trail down a karst canyon. The first 7 km end at the 11 m Veliki Buk waterfall, where kayaks are carried around on foot and lowered down, then a faster section runs over 1-5 m drops. Groups of 6 to 40 are accepted.

items.name: Zrmanja river rafting
items.description: A 14 km raft descent in boats of up to 8 people. A 14-person team splits into two rafts, which sets up a ready-made race. The big-raft season is October to mid-May, when the water is high, which makes this a true off-season activity.

items.name: Sea kayak around Zadar Old Town (half day)

location.name: Zadar peninsula: route Puntamika - Sea Organ - Riva - Foša (point = Sea Organ)

items.driveFromVilla: 20.9 km, about 27 min to the Sea Organ (OSRM)
items.description: A 3-hour paddle from Puntamika past the Sea Organ and the Greeting to the Sun, along the Riva with views of the Roman Forum and St Donatus, ending at Foša harbour by the old city gate. It pairs easily with an afternoon or evening in Zadar Old Town.

operators.name: Kayak Adventure Zadar (as listed on Manawa)

items.name: Team sailing regatta day from Zadar
items.driveFromVilla: about 20 km to Zadar (OSRM to the city centre: 21 km, 29 min)
items.description: Two or more chartered yachts race short legs along the Zadar coast, then the day ends at a beach bar. The Zadar Region Tourist Board promotes this as a flagship incentive. Bura and Jugo winds make it a real sailing challenge rather than a cruise.

items.name: Wine tasting and dinner at Kraljevski vinogradi (Royal Vineyards), Petrčane

location.name: Kraljevski vinogradi tasting room & konoba, Ulica XIII br. 10, Petrčane

items.description: The closest serious winery to the villa, in Petrčane near Punta Skala. It grows Pošip, Plavac Mali and Crljenak, and its tasting room and konoba explicitly host business gatherings and team buildings, which makes it a ready-made closing-night venue.

items.name: Organic wine and olive-oil tasting at Kotari (Maslina i vino cooperative, ex-MasVin), Polača
items.description: A guided cellar tour with 3 wines from EUR 15, or 3 wines, 2 extra-virgin olive oils and a cold platter for EUR 35. It is an organic cooperative in Ravni kotari, Croatia's largest coastal plain. The tasting room is open Monday to Saturday, 10:00-15:00, so it works as a late-morning stop on a hinterland day.

typicalPriceEUR.unit: per person, tasting 3 (3 wines, 2 olive oils, cold platter, sweet, guided tour); options from EUR 15

items.name: Škaulj organic winery tasting, Nadin
items.driveFromVilla: 40.0 km, about 50 min (OSRM, to Nadin village)
items.description: An award-winning organic winery in the centre of Nadin whose tasting facilities hold up to 50 people. The tourism board describes a lunch here of ham and cheese, meat and potatoes cooked under the peka, dessert and two eco-wines. Tastings are by prior arrangement only, which suits a small group booked in advance.

items.name: Wine and olive-oil tasting at Ražnjevića dvori AD 1307 estate
items.description: A restored rural estate dating back to 1307, with a guided tasting of 4 wines, olive oils, prosciutto, cheese and homemade bread. The tourism board lists it as a year-round tour by Ilirija Travel with return transport from Biograd or Zadar. It is also the start and finish point of a regional Bike and Wine tour.

operators.name: Ilirija Travel (Biograd na Moru), via the Zadar Region tourism board listing

items.name: Olive oil and wine tasting at OPG Mladen Dušević, Ražanac
items.driveFromVilla: 24.1 km, about 29 min (OSRM, to Ražanac village)
items.description: A family farm on the Velebit Channel coast where Mladen and Marijana Dušević serve their own olive oil and wine with local specialities. The farm address is not published, so the drive time is to Ražanac village centre; confirm the meeting point when you book. For a closer tasting, OPG Mate Dušević in Ljubač (about 11 km) offers olive-oil tastings and group meals.

items.name: Uljara Nadin olive mill tour and tasting
items.driveFromVilla: 40.0 km, about 50 min (OSRM, to Nadin village)
items.description: An olive mill with a tasting room and tours of the on-site production. It combines well with Škaulj winery in the same village for a half-day 'olive oil and wine' loop.

items.name: Guided walk through the Nin salt works (Solana Nin) and the Salt House museum
items.description: Free 45-60 minute guided walks through salt pans that are still hand-harvested, held on Open Days from June to September. English tours ran at 9:00, 11:00 and 17:00 in 2025. The fields can only be entered with a guide. It makes a good 7-minute 'field trip' between work blocks.

typicalPriceEUR.unit: free guided tour on Open Days

items.name: Guided or self-guided hike in Paklenica National Park (Velika Paklenica canyon)

location.name: NP Paklenica, entrance 1 Velika Paklenica, Starigrad

items.description: A limestone canyon walk below 400 m walls on the Velebit side of the Zadar channel. It is a classic shared-effort day out for a team. Spring and autumn are cooler and cheaper, with the adult day ticket at EUR 8 in March, April and October against EUR 10 from May to September.

typicalPriceEUR.unit: adult 1-day ticket in Mar/Apr/Oct (EUR 10 May-Sep, EUR 5 Nov-Feb); car vignette EUR 3-5

items.name: Velebit jeep safari

location.name: Velebit mountain (operator base Kruševo near Obrovac)

items.driveFromVilla: 64.2 km, about 70 min to the Riva Rafting Centar office (OSRM)
items.description: A 4x4 day on Velebit's rough tracks with viewpoints over the Adriatic. It is the tourism board's suggested team expedition, combined with a photo-hunt and a picnic of local cheese and cured meats.

items.name: Zadar Old Town scavenger hunt plus konoba cooking class

location.name: Zadar Old Town (Kalelarga / Forum / Five Wells)

items.description: Teams race through Kalelarga, the Five Wells square, the Varoš quarter, the markets and the UNESCO city walls. The day continues with a hands-on Dalmatian cooking class in a konoba and a Maraschino at sunset by the Sea Organ. The tourism board published this as its 'Zadar Uncovered' format.

items.name: ClueGo escape room, Zadar

location.name: Široka ulica 14, Zadar Old Town (address from Wanderlog only)

items.description: Escape rooms of 60 and 75 minutes in the Old Town: 'Anno', a 13th-century Crusader siege, and 'Morana', a fairy tale. With 2-5 players per room, a 10-14 person team splits into competing squads.

items.name: Full-day boat trip to Kornati National Park and Telašćica
items.driveFromVilla: about 21 km, about 27-30 min to the Zadar peninsula (OSRM)
items.description: Excursion boats leave Zadar in the morning for about 9 hours, cruising among the Kornati islets with meals on board, a swim stop and Telašćica's salt lake. Whether the national park tickets are included depends on the product, so check before booking.

typicalPriceEUR.unit: per person, shared excursion boat, 'from EUR 49.99' on the Croatica Rezdy page; ticket-inclusive versions are listed higher (about USD 68 on Expedia)

items.name: 'Life on Mars' guided night hike on Pag's lunar karst

location.name: Ručica beach near Novalja, Pag island

items.driveFromVilla: 88.7 km, about 1 h 42 min to Ručica beach via the Pag bridge (OSRM)
items.description: A guided 3-hour night hike from Ručica beach over bare, wind-scoured limestone to Beritnica beach and its bura-shaped rocks, the Stogaj rock column and Slana bay. It is open from age 8 with an adult. Travel writers recommend March to May, because summer heat on the shadeless karst passes 30°C.

items.name: Private chef dinner at the villa (Take a Chef marketplace)

location.name: At the villa (chef travels from the Zadar area)

items.description: Request menus from about 48 Zadar-area private chefs. The chef cooks on site, for example a Croatian BBQ sharing menu on the villa grill, so the team never leaves the terrace on the big-dinner night. Published per-guest tiers fall as the group grows, to EUR 64 per guest for 7-12 and EUR 63 for 13 or more.

typicalPriceEUR.unit: per guest for 7-12 guests (EUR 63 for 13+), platform average 'everything included'

items.name: Peka cooking class in a home setting, Ninski Stanovi
items.driveFromVilla: 7.1 km, about 10 min (OSRM, to the village)
items.description: Watch meat and vegetables slow-cook under the peka, the iron bell traditionally covered in embers, make kroštule dough, then eat the peka dinner. It is 10 minutes from the villa and suits a hands-on team evening.

operators.name: Listed on byFood (host name not retrieved)

items.name: Berekin Catering (Konoba Berekin)

location.name: Ul. Hrvatskog Sabora 12G (per Wanderlog; town ambiguous)

items.description: A Zadar event venue and caterer known for weddings, with a venue of over 70 seats. It is a lead for a catered welcome dinner or a working-lunch delivery, if it delivers to villas.

items.name: Self-catered team BBQ at the villa grill and outdoor kitchen
items.description: The villa has a shared grill area and Apt 1's separate outdoor kitchen. A 'cook-off' BBQ, with teams shopping and grilling, is a zero-cost team activity and easily the most-remembered evening of many offsites.

items.name: COIN Coworking Zadar: multimedia hall for up to 25
items.description: A coworking space of about 370 m2 with roughly 35 workstations, run by the Zadar craftsmen's association. Its multimedia hall seats up to 25 with fast internet, projector and computer, plus recording and streaming. That makes it the backup venue for an all-hands video call or a client demo day when the villa's connection is not enough.

items.name: Code Hub Zadar (free EU-funded coworking)
items.description: A free 94 m2 coworking space with 25 places, one conference room and a kitchen, bookable through the Zoyya app. The whole space can be rented for dedicated events.

items.name: Congress & Event Center Zadar at Hotel Pinija, Petrčane
items.description: The nearest professional meeting venue, 15 minutes south. Rooms range from a 12-seat Business Corner (20 m2) and the 70-seat Foša hall to Riva (150), Forum (295) and Donat (355, theatre). It suits a day when a 14-person team brings in clients or a wider department.

items.name: Falkensteiner Resort Punta Skala conference centre

location.name: Falkensteiner Hotel & Spa Iadera, Punta Skala, Petrčane

items.description: A conference centre of over 600 m2 with seven combinable rooms, its own entrance and a business centre, plus the Ventus hall seating up to 470. It is mainly relevant as the fallback for a larger kick-off, or as a dinner and spa venue near the villa.

items.name: On-site work setup at the villa (terrace, balconies, 4 living rooms)
items.description: Four self-contained apartments act as four breakout rooms, with Apt 1's 68 m2 terrace and outdoor kitchen as the plenary and lunch space. That gives one main space plus 2-3 breakouts, the setup offsite planners recommend.

items.name: Mobile and fixed internet in Croatia (and how to check the villa)

location.name: Croatia (national figures); villa-specific check via HAKOM map

items.description: All three Croatian operators (A1, Hrvatski Telekom, Telemach) won national 5G licences in HAKOM's August 2021 auction (700 MHz, 3.6 GHz, 26 GHz) and offer commercial 5G. DataReportal puts Croatia's median mobile download at about 103 Mbps and fixed at about 80 Mbps at the end of 2025. HAKOM publishes per-operator coverage maps that guests can check for the villa address.

items.name: Zadar Airport (ZAD) arrival: shuttle bus or private transfer to the villa
items.driveFromVilla: 29.4 km, about 38 min to the passenger terminal (OSRM; OSRM durations are approximate)
items.description: Zadar Airport has had a Ryanair base since 2013 (reopened in 2021) and offers over 70 destinations in summer, according to Wikipedia. The Liburnija shuttle (about EUR 5, timed to arrivals) runs to Zadar bus station and the Old Town, but there is no direct bus to Nin or Sabunike. A team of 8-14 is best served by two rental cars or a pre-booked minibus.

typicalPriceEUR.unit: one-way airport shuttle to Zadar, per person

items.name: Nin lagoon healing mud (peloid) at Queen's Beach

location.name: Nin lagoon by Queen's Beach (Kraljičina plaža); point = beach polygon

items.driveFromVilla: 2.0 km, about 7 min to Queen's Beach (OSRM); walkable
items.description: Nin's lagoon next to Queen's Beach is described as Croatia's largest site of healing mud (peloid). Visitors traditionally coat themselves in the mud, dry in the sun on the sandy beach and rinse in the sea, mostly in summer. It is 2 km from the villa.

items.name: Acquapura Spa, Falkensteiner Hotel & Spa Iadera

location.name: Falkensteiner Hotel & Spa Iadera, Punta Skala

items.description: The nearest large hotel spa, with saunas open 10:00-21:00 and pools 08:00-22:00 according to the hotel FAQ. It is a candidate for a post-workshop recovery afternoon.

venueChecklist.question: How many people sleep in private bedrooms, and how many in total (beds, sofa beds)?
venueChecklist.why: The villa has 6 bedrooms. Teams of 8-14 must know upfront who shares.

venueChecklist.question: Measured Wi-Fi download and upload speed in each apartment, router per unit or a shared mesh, and is there a 4G/5G backup?
venueChecklist.why: Planners ask for upload speed, not just download, and want backup internet.

venueChecklist.question: Can the whole villa be booked exclusively, with no other guests on site?
venueChecklist.why: Exclusivity is a key reason small teams choose villas over hotels.

venueChecklist.question: Where is the plenary space for 14 (terrace or covered area), and is there a table seating 14, shade, and heating for April and October evenings?
venueChecklist.why: One main room plus breakouts is the standard offsite layout.

venueChecklist.question: Is there a screen, TV with HDMI, projector or whiteboard? Enough power outlets and extension leads?
venueChecklist.why: AV and power are basic venue requirements.

venueChecklist.question: Grill area and outdoor kitchen: seating capacity, can an outside chef or caterer use them, and are there kitchen limits?
venueChecklist.why: F&B is a top budget line, and teams want chef or catering flexibility.

venueChecklist.question: Which invoice can you issue: an R-1 with 13% VAT (VAT-registered business), or an invoice without VAT (private renter / paušalist)? Can you issue an eRačun to Croatian companies?
venueChecklist.why: Finance teams need to know whether VAT is deductible or reclaimable before approving.

venueChecklist.question: Tourist tax per person per night in Privlaka for 2026, and is it included in the quoted price?
venueChecklist.why: Avoids surprise line items on the company invoice.

venueChecklist.question: Parking spaces on the driveway (how many cars)?
venueChecklist.why: A team of 14 usually arrives in 3-4 rental cars or one minibus.

venueChecklist.question: Airport transfer: can you arrange or recommend a licensed minibus for 8-14 people from Zadar Airport?
venueChecklist.why: There is no direct public transport to Sabunike.

venueChecklist.question: Quiet hours, neighbours, and whether music or late group dinners are acceptable.
venueChecklist.why: Teams want both quiet for focus and freedom for a social evening.

venueChecklist.question: Off-season prices and minimum stay for a whole-villa booking (April-June, September-October), plus cancellation and force-majeure terms.
venueChecklist.why: Planners budget per person per day with contingency and negotiate cancellation terms.

venueChecklist.question: Step-free access to at least one apartment, and a quiet room.
venueChecklist.why: Accessibility and inclusivity checks are standard in planner guides.

venueChecklist.question: Nearest pharmacy, doctor and shop, and drive times to Nin, Zadar and the airport.
venueChecklist.status: partly answered: Nin 5.4 km / 9 min, Zadar 21 km / 29 min, ZAD 29 km / about 40 min (OSRM)

venueChecklist.question: Which nearby activities can you book on the team's behalf (kite school, SUP, wineries, chef), and do you take a commission?
venueChecklist.why: A direct host who arranges the programme is the main reason to skip a DMC.

whatCompaniesLookFor.detail: Reliable Wi-Fi plus backup internet. Ask for upload speed, not only download. Screens, microphones and recording if needed.
One main room plus 2-3 breakout rooms close together, with natural light. AV, power outlets and a layout that supports presentations and breakouts.
Exclusive use is worth it for groups under about 50, and private space supports confidential leadership discussions.
Senior staff often expect single rooms, so the room count must exceed the head count, or shared rooms must be stated upfront.
Proximity to a major airport, parking for those who drive, and a 2-3 h buffer on day one for delayed arrivals.
Dietary flexibility for working lunches and social dinners, and whether outside catering or a chef is allowed. F&B is one of the largest budget lines.
Outdoor spaces such as terraces, trails and fire pits where side conversations happen, plus an unstructured 90-minute window on day two.
Step-free access and a quiet or prayer space.
Per-person, per-day budgets with 10-15% contingency, transparent fees, and clear cancellation and force-majeure terms.

invoicingAndTax.fact: Croatia's standard VAT rate is 25%. Accommodation is taxed at the reduced rate of 13%, and catering services are also listed at 13%.

An 'R-1 račun' is the invoice a VAT-registered business issues, with VAT shown separately, so a business buyer can deduct input VAT. A supplier outside the VAT system issues an invoice without VAT (often called R-2), and the buyer has no VAT to deduct. Companies routinely ask for an 'R1 račun' by giving their OIB (11-digit tax number) and company name.

From 1 January 2026, VAT-registered businesses in Croatia must issue and receive structured e-invoices (eRačun) for domestic B2B transactions, with fiscalisation (Fiskalizacija 2.0). Non-VAT businesses such as flat-rate taxpayers (paušalisti) must be able to receive e-invoices from 2026, and the obligation to issue them is reported to start on 1 January 2027.

Foreign (non-Croatian) companies cannot deduct Croatian VAT in their home return. They reclaim it through the EU VAT refund procedure (or the non-EU 13th-directive route), which requires a valid invoice showing the supplier's Croatian VAT number.

Private holiday-rental hosts on flat-rate taxation (paušalni porez) must not be in the VAT system. Their invoices therefore carry no VAT, and a company booking them gets a valid expense invoice but no reclaimable VAT. One expert source warns that renting rooms to a legal entity is not 'residential letting', so the VAT position of company bookings should be checked with an accountant.
A tourist tax (turistička pristojba) is charged per person per night and set locally. The 2026 amount for Privlaka was not found.

offSeason.summary: April-June and September-October give warm days (17-26°C), sea at 14-22°C, quieter beaches, and price and availability advantages that can be shown with sources: Paklenica tickets are EUR 8 instead of EUR 10 in April and October, high Zrmanja water usually suits big rafts from October to May, and the kite school runs from May to late October. Some attractions are summer-only, such as the Solana Nin Open Days (June-September).
offSeason.climateNotes: These are weather2travel averages for Zadar. 'Rainy days' counts any day with some rain, so it overstates the disruption. Other sources differ by 1-2°C.

advantages.fact: NP Paklenica's 2026 adult day ticket is EUR 5 in Nov-Feb, EUR 8 in Mar/Apr/Oct and EUR 10 in May-Sep.
Big-raft trips on the Zrmanja run only with sufficient water, usually October to May, while summer suits kayaks.
Riva Rafting Centar sells a 6-day 'From the Sea to Velebit' active package only in April, September and October.
The Nin kite school runs from May to late October, and its high-season beach prices differ from advance-booking prices.
Pag's lunar karst is recommended in March-May, because summer heat on the shadeless trails exceeds 30°C.
Limitation: free Solana Nin guided tours run only on Open Days in June-September.
Zadar Airport's summer schedule starts at the end of March (30 March in 2025), so direct flights already run for April retreats. The winter network is much thinner and was not verified.

offSeason.villaPricing: Not researched. Off-season villa rates must come from the owner (see openQuestions).

openQuestions: Maximum occupancy and bed configuration per apartment (apt1-apt4), and the honest number of private bedrooms for a corporate group.
Wi-Fi provider, plan and measured download/upload speeds per apartment, and whether a mobile backup exists. Check the HAKOM coverage map for Put kandelica 60.

Whether the owner is VAT-registered (can issue an R-1 invoice with 13% VAT) or a flat-rate private renter (invoice without VAT), and readiness to issue eRačun to Croatian companies (mandatory for non-VAT issuers from 2027 per sources).
2026 tourist tax per person per night for Općina Privlaka.
Whole-villa off-season price, minimum nights and cancellation policy for April-June and September-October.
Seating capacity and lighting of the grill area, the Apt 1 outdoor kitchen, and whether an external chef may use them.
Number of parking spaces on the driveway.
Whether Kiteboarding Croatia offers closed group sessions for 8-14 and the instructor-to-student ratio.
Whether Solana Nin offers private group tours outside Open Days, and the 2026 English tour times.
Whether ClueGo still operates in Zadar in 2026, with its address and group pricing.
Whether Hotel Pinija's Congress & Event Center or Falkensteiner Punta Skala rent rooms by the day to non-resident groups, and at what rate.
Whether the Falkensteiner Iadera spa sells day passes to non-residents.
A verified corporate sailing-regatta operator in Zadar (none found), and a verified minibus or transfer company for 8-14 people from ZAD.
Verified local yoga, massage or wellness providers who come to the villa (none found).
Kraljevski vinogradi group tasting prices, capacity and opening months.
Exact location of the Nin healing-mud area (the OSM Queen's Beach polygon is used as a stand-in), and whether ClueGo Zadar still operates at Široka ulica 14.
Whether Konoba Berekin / Berekin Catering exists in Sabunike/Privlaka (OSM has a Ulica Hrvatskog sabora 600 m from the villa) or in Zadar, and whether it caters to villas.
